column4: Real talk: the hardest part of investing is not the charts. It is the person holding the phone. That is you. Fear and greed will try to run your money, and honestly, they are really convincing. This lesson is about beating them with two boring, unstoppable tools: a plan, and a journal. Let's build the discipline that separates a trader from a gambler.

Meet the two villains: fear and greed. Look at the dial. When a stock is ripping and everyone is hyped, greed whispers buy now, do not miss out, and you buy high. Then when it drops and everyone panics, fear screams sell, get out, and you sell low. Buy high, sell low, the exact opposite of the plan. Feelings are loud, and they are usually wrong at the worst possible moment.

Here is the fix: a written plan. Watch the chart. The red line is the emotional trader, buying at the top out of greed, selling at the bottom out of fear, getting whipsawed all over the place. The green line is you with a plan: your entry, your exit, and your stop, all decided before you click anything. When the plan is written down first, feelings do not get a vote. That steady green line is what discipline actually looks like.

And this is your secret weapon: the journal. Every trade, you write it down. Why you got in, your plan, your exit, your stop, and what actually happened. Then you review it. The journal is a mirror. It shows you your real patterns, the mistakes you keep repeating, and the setups that actually work for you. It is basically your own coach, and it works for free.

Try it yourself. Drag the dial from extreme fear all the way to extreme greed. Watch what the emotional move would be at each point, and what the calm, plan-following move is instead. Feel the gap between them.
Now sort these. Some are plan moves, the calm disciplined choice. Some are feelings moves, driven by fear or greed. Tap one, then drop it in the right column.
Five questions. Show me you can keep your cool and trust the plan.

So that is the inner game. Fear and greed will always show up, but a written plan and an honest journal keep them from running your money. Remember, small losses are wins, because they protect you for the next shot. Next up is the finale: the first-trade checklist, where every single thing you have learned becomes one written plan before you ever click buy.
